title: Mildred Bailey and Billie Holiday's mother; adjusting to the swing era; end
summary: Mildred Bailey recorded "Downhearted Blues"; Hunter doesn't believe Albertson's story that she hired Billie's mother as a maid out of jealousy. Albertson asks whether the changing style of the 1940s caused problems; the recording ends as she begins to answer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Did you ever meet Mildred Bailey?
Yes. Oh, she was a darling.
Yes. Mildred could sing awhile. She made a lovely record of 'Downhearted Blues'.
I've heard that she was very jealous of Billie Holiday.
And that she was so jealous of Billie Holiday that, to spite her, she hired Billie's mother to be her maid.
No. I don't believe it. Mildred was
a good hearted girl. I don't -- is she still living?
Bless her heart. Well, I don't believe that. It could be true, but I don't believe it.

Now, did you have a -- when you started singing, you know, it was so long ago, and by the time you got to the '40s, for instance, we were going into the swing era, and the whole style of the music had changed.
